successCriteria.description: The test file tests/unit/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.service.test.ts imports LeavePolicy from the leave-policy module's public barrel (index.ts) rather than from the internal model file, and no direct import of any leave-policy internal file remains in that test file.

The finalizeDeduction method in src/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.service.ts computes the new pendingDays value with a Math.max(0, balance.pendingDays - days) floor so that pendingDays can never become negative, matching the defensive pattern already present in releaseReservation.

All existing unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.service.test.ts continue to pass after both edits, including the two finalizeDeduction tests (3→0 and 20→20) whose expected results are unchanged by the Math.max floor.
The project type-checks cleanly (tsc --noEmit) after the import consolidation, confirming LeavePolicy is type-equivalent whether imported from the barrel or the internal model file.

constraints: Modules (and their tests) must import from each other ONLY through the declared public entry point (index.ts barrel), never from internal files — per AGENTS.md architecture rule 1 and ARCHITECTURE.md dependency rules. The LeavePolicy import in the test file must come from the leave-policy barrel, not from leave-policy.model.ts.

The pendingDays floor must be applied at the single occurrence of the pendingDays decrement inside finalizeDeduction (the line computing balance.pendingDays - days), not at any other location; the usedDays increment (balance.usedDays + days) is unchanged.
No new test cases are required for this phase — the edits must not break existing tests. Adding a test for the days > pendingDays negative case is permitted but not mandated by this phase's scope.
outOfScope: Refactoring or altering any other method in LeaveBalanceService (reserveDays, releaseReservation, getAvailableBalance, initializeBalancesForEmployee, getBalancesForEmployee) beyond the targeted finalizeDeduction pendingDays floor.

Changing the LeaveBalanceService source-file imports (src/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.service.ts already imports correctly from the leave-policy barrel); only the test file's import is consolidated.
Modifying the leave-policy barrel (index.ts) or the LeavePolicy model — the barrel already re-exports LeavePolicy; no change is needed there.

entityInvariants.invariant: pendingDays must never be driven below zero by any balance-mutating operation. The finalizeDeduction operation (which moves pendingDays to usedDays on approval) must enforce this floor just as releaseReservation already does, so that an over-deduction (days > pendingDays) clamps pendingDays to 0 rather than producing a negative value.

remainingDays is a computed field equal to totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays; the pendingDays floor in finalizeDeduction preserves the consistency of this computation by preventing negative pendingDays from inflating remainingDays beyond totalEntitlement - usedDays.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws AppError with code NOT_FOUND when no balance record exists for the given employee/policy/fiscal-year triple. On success, atomically updates the balance in a single repository update call: pendingDays is set to Math.max(0, balance.pendingDays - days) and usedDays is set to balance.usedDays + days. The pendingDays result must never be negative.

Throws AppError with code NOT_FOUND when no balance record exists. On success, sets pendingDays to Math.max(0, balance.pendingDays - days) and does not alter usedDays. This is the reference defensive pattern that finalizeDeduction must match.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The pendingDays floor in finalizeDeduction must reuse the exact defensive pattern already established in releaseReservation within the same service file: compute the new pendingDays via Math.max(0, balance.pendingDays - days) before calling the repository update, rather than inlining the raw subtraction.

The consolidated LeavePolicy import in the test file must resolve to the same type exported by the leave-policy barrel, which re-exports LeavePolicy from the internal model — ensuring type-equivalence and no behavioral change.

The test file's barrel import must remain consistent with the source service file's existing barrel import pattern: both import ILeavePolicyService and AppError (and now LeavePolicy) from the leave-policy public entry point, never from internal module files.

integrationPoints.why: The test file consumes the LeavePolicy type via this barrel; the barrel must re-export LeavePolicy (it already does) so the consolidated import resolves correctly.
finalizeDeduction persists the floored pendingDays and incremented usedDays through a single update call; the repository contract for atomic field updates must be respected.
